less_stable.text: When opponents play a net shot to Zhao's front forehand, Zhao loses the point within two shots 7% of the time (n=105, 95% CI 3%-13%); typical pros lose 13% after the same shot (difference -7 points, 95% CI -10 to 0, n=7056).

possible.title: When opponents play a net shot to Zhao's front forehand:
possible.detail: possibly less costly than for typical pros (7% vs 13%, n=105); the 95% interval on the difference touches zero once rounded to whole points (-10 to 0).

insight.text: When opponents play a net shot to Zhao's front forehand, Zhao loses the point within two shots 7% of the time (n=105, 95% CI 3%-13%); typical pros lose 13% after the same shot (difference -7 points, 95% CI -10 to 0, n=7056).

coach.possible_note: The 95% interval on the difference excludes zero by less than half a point, so printed to whole points it touches zero: a lead, not a finding.

frame.x: metres from the centre line toward the player's own right
frame.y: metres from the net into the player's own half

xp.caveat: Read this first: xP from shot and position data has no signal mid-rally in elite singles (holdout AUC 0.50 on strokes that did not end the rally). The same features reach AUC 0.79 only on final strokes, where the task is classifying how an already-decisive stroke ends (winner or error), not predicting a rally. Nothing in this section is a working expected-points model.
